results.title: Ministerial Statement on COVID-19 Testing and Pre-Event Protocols
results.content: Minister Gan Kim Yong addressed Parliament on the progression to Phase Three and the role of pre-event testing in enabling higher-risk activities including weddings to scale up safely. He explained how antigen rapid tests can return fairly accurate results quickly, within half an hour, while noting they are not as accurate as PCR tests.
results.summary: Minister outlines pre-event testing strategy to enable safer resumption of high-risk gatherings during Phase Three reopening.
results.speaker: Minister for Health Gan Kim Yong

results.title: Parliamentary Question: TraceTogether Token Distribution Timeline
results.content: Member Lim Biow Chuan asked the Prime Minister regarding the timeline of TraceTogether token distribution to seniors and accessibility concerns for citizens without smartphones. Minister responded that 570,000 tokens had been issued as of November 1st, with distribution prioritized in areas with higher elderly populations.
results.summary: Parliament receives update on TraceTogether token rollout progress and accessibility measures for vulnerable populations.
results.speaker: Parliamentary Members

results.title: Live-Streaming of Parliament Proceedings Commences
results.content: Minister S Iswaran announced the commencement of live-streaming of Parliamentary proceedings on MCI's YouTube channel, with two streams available—one with English interpretation of vernacular speeches and one without. The move enhances transparency while preserving parliamentary dignity and debate quality.
results.summary: Government launches live-streaming of Parliament proceedings to enhance public transparency and engagement.
results.speaker: Minister for Communications and Information S Iswaran

results.title: COVID-19 Vaccination Programme Rollout and Safety Framework
results.content: The Health Sciences Authority provided details on COVID-19 vaccine assessment criteria and the Safety and Efficacy framework established to ensure appropriate and safe vaccination for Singapore residents. Multiple Members sought clarification on side effects, vaccination card provisions, and rollout timelines.
results.summary: Parliament receives comprehensive briefing on COVID-19 vaccination programme implementation and safety protocols.
results.speaker: Minister for Health

results.title: High Speed Rail Project Termination and Compensation Framework
results.content: Minister Ong Ye Kung announced the termination of the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High Speed Rail project following Malaysia's decision not to proceed. Singapore incurred over S$270 million in abortive costs, with compensation terms specified in the bilateral agreement. The Minister explained that fundamental disagreements over the Assets Company role led to the impasse.
results.summary: Government announces termination of HSR project and details compensation arrangements with Malaysia.
results.speaker: Minister for Transport Ong Ye Kung

results.title: Parliamentary Question: Data Protection and Information Security in PDPA Context
results.content: Member Christopher de Souza questioned the use of TraceTogether data for criminal investigations, seeking clarification on legal safeguards and data protection frameworks. Minister Desmond Tan confirmed that Singapore Police Force can obtain TT data under the Criminal Procedure Code with stringent safeguards including authorization requirements and penalties for unauthorized disclosure.
results.summary: Parliament examines data protection safeguards in law enforcement use of contact tracing data.
results.speaker: Member Christopher de Souza and Minister Desmond Tan

results.title: Strengthening the Singaporean Core: Fair Hiring Practices and PMET Protection
results.content: Member Patrick Tay highlighted concerns about fair consideration for Singaporean PMEs and proposed strengthening hiring culture and practices through mentoring, diversity initiatives, and anti-discrimination enforcement. He emphasized the need for a two-fold approach: merit-based hiring of foreign workers and equipping local workers with relevant skills.
results.summary: Parliament debates strategies to protect Singaporean professionals amid foreign worker competition and economic uncertainty.
results.speaker: Member Patrick Tay Teck Guan

results.title: Parliamentary Question: Net Investment Returns Contribution to Budget
results.content: Member Chua Kheng Wee Louis asked the Deputy PM and Minister for Finance regarding the percentage of Net Investment Returns and Net Investment Income contributing to the Budget. Minister Lawrence Wong confirmed that FY2016-2020 utilized the maximum 50% allowable under the Constitution, with similar approach planned for FY2021.
results.summary: Parliament receives update on fiscal management and investment returns contribution framework.
results.speaker: Member Chua Kheng Wee Louis and Minister Lawrence Wong

results.title: GST Voucher Scheme and Progressive Taxation Framework
results.content: Minister Lawrence Wong outlined the comprehensive GST Voucher scheme structure, noting that the permanent GSTV scheme offsets an average of 84% of annual GST payable by the bottom 20% of Singaporean households. Special payments in 2019-2020 provided additional offset equivalent to 33% of GST payable.
results.summary: Government details progressive social support mechanisms to offset regressive consumption taxes.
results.speaker: Minister for Finance Lawrence Wong

results.title: Manpower Crisis in Construction, Marine and Process Sectors
results.content: Minister Tan See Leng addressed the manpower shortage in CMP sectors following COVID-related worker repatriation. From November 2020 to April 2021, 5,100 S Pass and Work Permit holders were granted entry monthly. Government increased foreign worker levy rebates from 90 to 250 per holder to enable employers to hire workers from alternative sources including China.
results.summary: Parliament hears update on government measures to address critical manpower shortages in essential sectors.
results.speaker: Minister for Manpower Dr Tan See Leng

results.title: After-Action Review on COVID-19 Response Rather Than Commission of Inquiry
results.content: Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean explained the government's decision to conduct a comprehensive after-action review (AAR) rather than a Commission of Inquiry into COVID-19 response. He emphasized that AAR allows participants to be open and reflective, while a COI's quasi-judicial nature would not suit the evolving, ongoing nature of pandemic management.
results.summary: Government outlines accountability framework for COVID-19 pandemic response through after-action review process.
results.speaker: Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean

results.title: Global Minimum Corporate Tax Rate and Impact on Singapore
results.content: Minister Lawrence Wong presented detailed analysis of G7 agreement on global minimum corporate tax rate of 15%, explaining Pillar One (reallocation of taxing rights to customer locations) and Pillar Two (minimum effective tax rate floor). He noted approximately 1,800 MNE groups in Singapore would meet the revenue criterion and expected majority to have effective tax rates below 15%.
results.summary: Government briefs Parliament on implications of international tax reform on Singapore's tax competitiveness.
results.speaker: Minister for Finance Lawrence Wong

results.title: Parliamentary Question: Free Trade Agreements and Employment Outcomes
results.content: Multiple Members posed questions on the India-Singapore CECA and other FTAs, seeking analysis of net economic benefits for trade, value-added growth, and employment outcomes for Singaporeans. Minister responded that comprehensive analysis would be provided through Ministerial Statements addressing broader questions on trade outcomes.
results.summary: Parliament seeks accountability on employment and economic outcomes from free trade commitments.
results.speaker: Parliamentary Members and Ministers

results.title: Make-Up Pay Mechanism for Political Appointment Holders
results.content: Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean explained the make-up pay mechanism introduced in 1989 to ease financial transition for candidates from private sector joining political office. The scheme has been used once for a two-year transition period. Government emphasized that sense of public service remains the primary recruitment criterion.
results.summary: Government explains compensation framework for attracting private sector talent into political office.
results.speaker: Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean

results.title: PLAAF Aircraft Transit Through Singapore FIR and Air Defence Protocols
results.content: Minister Ng Eng Hen clarified Singapore's handling of 16 PLA Air Force aircraft that transited through Singapore's Flight Information Region on 31 May 2021. He distinguished between military passage rights under UNCLOS, civilian air traffic management by CAAS, and SAF air defence responsibilities, emphasizing Singapore's impartial approach to all countries.
results.summary: Defence Minister addresses parliamentary concerns about foreign military aircraft transits through Singapore airspace.
results.speaker: Minister for Defence Dr Ng Eng Hen

results.title: Budget 2022: Progressive Taxation and Social Support Measures
results.content: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong presented Budget 2022 focused on fair and progressive measures. The budget includes enhanced GST Voucher schemes with permanent assistance, Progressive Wage Model for low-wage workers, carbon tax introduction, and corporate tax adjustments aligned with international standards. Focus on strengthening Singaporean core and green economy transition.
results.summary: Government delivers transformative budget with emphasis on fairness, sustainability, and support for vulnerable workers.
results.speaker: Deputy PM and Minister for Finance Lawrence Wong

results.title: Cycling Safety Infrastructure and Road User Education
results.content: Minister Chee Hong Tat discussed comprehensive approach to cycling safety combining infrastructure improvements, public education, and enforcement. He noted conversion of open drains to wider footpaths in Toa Payoh and emphasized shared responsibility between different road users—motorists must respect cyclist vulnerability.
results.summary: Parliament addresses cycling safety through multi-pronged infrastructure and education approach.
results.speaker: Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat

results.title: Parliamentary Question: Working Mothers Child Relief and Parenthood Tax Rebate
results.content: Member Louis Ng Kok Kwang raised concerns about excluding single unwed parents from Working Mothers Child Relief and Parenthood Tax Rebate. Minister Indranee Rajah acknowledged government support for all children regardless of marital status but noted these measures were designed to encourage work within marriage context and reflect prevailing societal values.
results.summary: Parliament debates tax policy regarding single parents and inclusiveness in social support frameworks.
results.speaker: Member Louis Ng Kok Kwang and Minister Indranee Rajah

results.title: Corruption Investigation into Minister S Iswaran
results.content: Parliament received notification of CPIB formal investigation into Minister S Iswaran on 11 July 2023. Multiple Members posed questions about investigation procedures, disclosure timelines, and transparency protocols. Prime Minister indicated Minister would be on leave of absence during investigation.
results.summary: Parliament addresses transparency and accountability in investigation of political office holder.
results.speaker: Parliamentary Members and Government Ministers

results.title: Speaker Resignation and Election of New Speaker Seah Kian Peng
results.content: Tan Chuan-Jin resigned as Speaker of Parliament on 17 July 2023. Seah Kian Peng was subsequently elected as the 11th Speaker. In his acceptance address, he emphasized commitment to fair, firm and impartial conduct of parliamentary proceedings and stressed importance of parliamentary conduct both inside and outside the Chamber.
results.summary: Parliament conducts Speaker election following resignation, emphasizing governance and decorum standards.
results.speaker: Parliamentary Leadership

results.title: Parliamentary Conduct and Decorum Reminder Following Leong Mun Wai Incident
results.content: Leader of the House Ms Indranee Rajah issued formal reminder on parliamentary conduct following Leong Mun Wai's March statements. She highlighted rules requiring respect for Chair authority, substantiation of allegations, and avoidance of scandalous statements about Parliament or Members. Distributed guidance note on relevant provisions of Parliament Privileges Act.
results.summary: Parliament reinforces conduct rules and standards following member's controversial public statements.
results.speaker: Leader of the House Indranee Rajah

results.title: Regulatory Framework for Energy Market and TRECS Scheme
results.content: Minister Dr Tan See Leng addressed concerns about the Transitional Energy Credit Support (TRECS) scheme and electricity market stability. He confirmed standby LNG facility support for gencos and noted over-subscription of TRECS in certain months, with measures to enhance energy security through diversified fuel supply arrangements.
results.summary: Government addresses energy market concerns and outlines regulatory support mechanisms.
results.speaker: Minister for Trade and Industry Dr Tan See Leng

results.title: China-Singapore Bilateral Cooperation and Digital Economy Partnership
results.content: Minister of State Low Yen Ling elaborated on outcomes of 19th Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation meeting with China, highlighting 24 deliverables across trade, renewable energy, digital economy, and finance. Noted potential for Singapore companies in China's digital economy and opportunities for growth in emerging sectors.
results.summary: Government outlines expanded economic partnership opportunities with China in digital and green sectors.
results.speaker: Minister of State Low Yen Ling

results.title: Public Housing Policy and Social Mobility Framework
results.content: Speaker Seah Kian Peng discussed HDB housing as foundation of Singapore's Social Compact, noting first-time homebuyers can receive grants up to S$80,000 for new flats or S$160,000 for resale units. Emphasized housing as enabler of self-reliance and social mobility, alongside education and healthcare investments.
results.summary: Parliament affirms public housing as key component of social mobility and equitable development.
results.speaker: Speaker Seah Kian Peng

results.title: Parliamentary Question: NFT Income Tax Treatment
results.content: Member Yip Hon Weng asked Minister Lawrence Wong about income tax treatment for non-fungible token transactions. Minister confirmed that prevailing income tax rules apply based on nature and use of NFT, with persons deriving income from NFT transactions subject to income tax, though capital gains treatment may apply in certain circumstances.
results.summary: Parliament receives tax guidance on emerging digital asset class transactions.
results.speaker: Member Yip Hon Weng and Minister Lawrence Wong

results.title: Parliamentary Question: Transport Connectivity for Fernvale Residents
results.content: Member Baey Yam Keng outlined public transport services available to Fernvale residents including Light Rail Transit connections to Sengkang town centre, regular bus services to surrounding towns, and City Direct Service 671 providing peak-hour connectivity to the city. LTA continues enhancements aligned with new housing developments.
results.summary: Parliament receives update on public transport infrastructure supporting new housing developments.
results.speaker: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng

results.title: Parliamentary Question: Support for Single Unwed Parents
results.content: Member Louis Ng raised follow-up questions on single unwed parent support, asking whether divorced persons qualify for tax rebates. Minister committed to continued support for vulnerable single parents through social service channels while noting tax measures reflect societal values and original policy intent.
results.summary: Parliament continues debate on inclusivity of social support systems for non-traditional family structures.
results.speaker: Member Louis Ng Kok Kwang and Minister Indranee Rajah

results.title: Opening of Second Session Parliament: Presidential Address
results.content: President Halimah delivered Opening Address highlighting themes of adaptation to different world realities, importance of national unity amid greater parliamentary diversity, and commitment to continued social progress. Noted 31 newly elected MPs including largest Opposition contingent in recent history and need for constructive debate.
results.summary: President addresses Parliament on national priorities and legislative agenda for new session.
results.speaker: President Halimah Yacob

results.title: Ministerial Statement on Opposition Leader Designation
results.content: Leader of the House Indranee Rajah formally announced designation of Pritam Singh as Leader of the Opposition, with accompanying privileges including opposite seating to Prime Minister, parliamentary office, staff support, extended speaking duration (40 minutes), and right of first response on lead questions to Ministers.
results.summary: Parliament formalizes Opposition Leader role with accompanying parliamentary privileges and resources.
results.speaker: Leader of the House Ms Indranee Rajah

results.title: Budget 2024: Cost of Living and Household Support Measures
results.content: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong presented Budget 2024 focused on managing cost of living amid global inflation. Measures include U-Save and Service and Conservancy Charges rebates, Community Development Council vouchers, and continuation of household support schemes to help Singaporeans navigate higher prices for food, electricity, and essential services.
results.summary: Government addresses inflation through targeted household support and rebate programmes.
results.speaker: Deputy PM Lawrence Wong
